>In this notebook, I present results of the pilot study ran between 9^th^ and
26^th^ June 2026 via JATOS on <https://mindprobe.eu>.

# The experiment

The study design was identical to the @beesley2011 replication of the
three-stage forward blocking via allergy task described in the main text. The
experimental code is recorded in the `catlaslab` repository under its release
from 19^th^ June 2026
(<https://github.com/josefmana/catlaslab/releases/tag/fba-allergy-online-01>).

::: {.callout-note title="Patch of June the 10^th^"}
The first wave of data collection (9^th^&mdash;16^th^ June) which yielded four
full data responses, included a minor bug in debriefing variables naming that
was patched for the remaining participants. Consequently, the first four
participants' data live in a different Mindprobe instance from the rest of the
sample. However, since the code change does not alter the experimental data,
data from both of these runs are treated identically in the following.
:::

# Participants

## Exclusion criteria

::: {.callout-warning title="Learning checks"}
Here, all participants that completed the experiment in full are included, and
I do not apply any *a priori* learning checks to filter participants out. This
decision is part of piloting. During data exploration, I aim to implement
learning checks calculations, document them, and explore how changing their
thresholds may or may not affect results. The exclusion-related goal of this
study is to set-up reasonable learning-based exclusion criteria by exploring
their impact on results in the pilot data set, so that the criteria can then be
pre-registered for ensuing experiments.
:::
